# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This website hosts the materials for **From Pixels to Policy**, a one-day, hands-on hackathon where you'll brainstorm and code your way through some of the most pressing **heat and greenspace challenges** facing a UK city region.

The hackathon is organised by [**Imago: Data Service for Imagery**](https://imago.ac.uk/) in collaboration with the [**Earth Observation Data Hub (EODH)**](https://eodatahub.org.uk/) and the **North East Data Network (DataNEt)** at [**Insights North East (INE)**](https://insightsnortheast.co.uk/). It brings together local authority professionals, policy experts and data/technical practitioners to explore how satellite imagery and Earth observation (EO) data can inform local responses to **urban heat**, **greenspace** and **unequal exposure** in **Newcastle and the wider North East**.

## Who is this for? {.unnumbered}

**Policy & public sector participants.** Local authority officers, policy makers and public health practitioners interested in new data sources, or in fresh ways of working with environmental and spatial data. You don't need to code — your knowledge of how decisions actually get made is what turns a map into a policy.

**Technical participants.** Data scientists, programmers and GIS/geographic data specialists who want to collaborate on practical, hands-on data challenges using Earth observation products from Imago and the EODH.

Teams are deliberately mixed so that every group combines policy and operational knowledge with analytical capability.

## Register {.unnumbered}

Registration is through [**Eventbrite**](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/from-pixels-to-policy-an-earth-observation-hackathon-tickets-2003542936858). Places are limited so that teams stay small and balanced.

To find out more, contact **Brigid Bell** at [brigid.bell\@liverpool.ac.uk](mailto:brigid.bell@liverpool.ac.uk).
